title: Fourier coefficients of the odd slice
statement: Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional sign cube, and define its odd part in the first coordinate by half the difference of its slices at first-coordinate signs $+1$ and $-1$. For every subset $S$ of the remaining $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient of this odd part at $S$ equals the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at the set consisting of the first coordinate together with the corresponding subset of the last $n$ coordinates.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional sign cube
$S$ is a subset of the remaining $n$ coordinates
